extracted.intended_audience: Macaulay2 package authors and contributors writing documentation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authoring Macaulay2 documentation nodes using the SimpleDoc package: format, available helper functions/templates, and formatting conventions (notably indentation/off-side rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-readable text format
rubrics_metrics.description: SimpleDoc provides a simple, human-readable text format for documentation nodes as an alternative to the classic hypertext list format accepted by the document(List) function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer authoring documentation in the SimpleDoc plain-text format to produce readable documentation nodes rather than the older hypertext/list representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted by doc(String) for single or multiple nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: The new format is accepted by the doc(String) function for writing either a single or multiple documentation nodes from a string or file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing documentation strings/files in SimpleDoc format, use doc(String) (or multidoc) to load one or more documentation nodes into Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the off-side rule (indentation defines blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: SimpleDoc adheres to the off-side rule, i.e., using indentation to separate blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure documentation by indentation levels: block boundaries and nesting are determined by consistent indentation rather than explicit delimiters. Ensure indentation is consistent to convey block structure correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided templates and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The package supplies templates and example documentation nodes (docExample, docTemplate, packageTemplate) and helper links (arXiv, stacksProject, wikipedia) to help construct documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the supplied templates (e.g., packageTemplate(String)) and examples as patterns for writing documentation nodes; use helper functions for consistent linking to external resources.
